subject: A modal-synthesis schematic: a mallet impulse driving a bank of four tuned resonators through a shared glaze dashpot into a summing junction, with the bowl's ringing output trace on the right.
controls: strike: shape — the impulse in the mallet block narrows from a wide soft pulse (16 px) to a sharp spike (2 px) and grows taller; column 1, left zone.
glaze: position — the dashpot piston sinks ~40 px into its cylinder, the damper engaging every resonator; column 2, left zone.
crack: shape — the output trace's envelope breaks into beating lobes (amplitude dips up to 80 %) and its cycles go uneven; column 3, right zone.
fire: position — the mode ruler's ticks under the trace spread right as the modes stretch (top tick travels ~30 px), and the resonator labels' ratios follow in the header-free bank.
risks: Most at risk of reading as a dashboard: boxes, a slider-like dashpot and a ruler are panel furniture unless the schematic stays drawn in one hairline language with the trace the only bright thing. fire on a tick ruler is thin (1.5 px ticks) and may score under its floor; it may need the trace's cycle spacing too, which collides with crack on the trace's shape. The trace transient is noisy at 64 points: one mutable path can't hold this many cycles, so a real build shows fewer cycles or uses 2–3 paths. Text in the resonator boxes changes with fire, which needs text slots.
